name: Panama
summary: Panama offers permanent residence by investment (Qualified Investor: USD 300,000 for a new first-sale property, USD 500,000 for resale or securities, from 16 September 2026) and a Friendly Nations visa (USD 200,000, about 50 listed nationalities incl. the US and most EU states, 2 years provisional first). Retirees need a USD 1,000 monthly pension; remote workers USD 36,000 a year. US, EU and other passports are treated alike except for the Friendly Nations list.
naturalisation: Five years of permanent residence (three for spouses of Panamanians), Spanish test and civics exam, solvency and clean record. Shorter periods for some nationalities by reciprocity.
dual_citizenship_note: Sources disagree: one says dual citizenship only with reciprocity countries, another that it is restricted on paper but rarely enforced. Check with a Panamanian lawyer.

routes.name: Qualified Investor visa (permanent residence)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for a property, securities or bank-deposit investment. From 16 September 2026 resale property needs USD 500,000; only a new first-sale property still qualifies at USD 300,000.
routes.requirements: Executive Decree 17 of 8 September 2026 (rules apply from 16 September 2026; earlier filings and binding contracts signed before then may use old thresholds if filed within 6 months). Options: new first-sale real estate USD 300,000; resale real estate USD 500,000; promise-of-sale USD 300,000 backed by an irrevocable bank instrument (max 3 cumulative years); securities USD 500,000 held 5 years; fixed deposit USD 750,000 in a private bank or USD 500,000 in Banco Nacional or Caja de Ahorros, held 5 years. Funds must be the applicant's own foreign-source funds, not a gift from an unrelated party. Annual evidence to MICI. A second source dates the rise to 15 October 2026 and describes the decree differently; treat the exact date as unconfirmed.
routes.physical_presence: One visit every two years is cited by secondary sources; not confirmed

sources.title: Qualified Investor Visa in Panama: Executive Decree No. 17 of 8 September 2026
Panama Residency for Investors: the October 2026 deadline

routes.investment_options: First-sale real estate USD 300,000; resale real estate USD 500,000; securities USD 500,000; fixed deposit USD 750,000 (private bank) or USD 500,000 (state banks).
routes.tax_note: Panama taxes only Panama-source income (territorial); permanent residence alone does not decide tax residence (183 days test).

routes.name: Friendly Nations visa
routes.summary: Residence for nationals of about 50 'friendly' countries (including the US and most EU states) who buy USD 200,000 of property, lock a USD 200,000 deposit for 3 years, or hold a formal local job. Starts with 2 years of provisional residence.
routes.requirements: Nationals of about 50 countries (US, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan and 'most of the EU'; the list was not read). One economic tie: real estate of USD 200,000, a fixed deposit of USD 200,000 for 3 years in a general-licence bank, or formal employment with a Panamanian company with a MITRADEL work permit. After 2 years provisional, apply for permanent residence. The sources describe the 2026 changes only vaguely; a possible stricter economic-link test was reported but not confirmed. Not open to nationals outside the friendly list.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed

sources.title: Panama's Friendly Nations Visa: the 2026 guide

routes.processing_time: Provisional approval 3 to 6 months, permanent step 2 to 4 months (secondary source)
routes.tax_note: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxed.

routes.name: Pensionado (retiree) visa
routes.summary: Permanent residence for retirees with a lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month.
routes.requirements: Lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month (USD 12,000 a year), plus USD 250 a month per dependant; USD 750 a month if the applicant owns Panamanian real estate worth over USD 100,000. Couples may combine pensions per one source. A visit every two years is cited to keep the status.
routes.physical_presence: A visit every two years (secondary source)
routes.tax_note: Pensionado holders also get discounts (not researched). Panama taxes only Panama-source income.

routes.name: Short Stay Remote Worker visa
routes.summary: A 9-month visa, renewable once, for remote workers earning at least USD 36,000 a year from outside Panama.
routes.requirements: Foreign-source income of at least USD 36,000 a year (USD 3,000 a month); contract with a foreign transnational company or self-employed teleworking; valid medical insurance covering Panama. Created by Executive Decree 198 of 7 May 2021. Valid 9 months, renewable once for the same period. Cancelled if the holder represents the foreign company in local activities.
routes.physical_presence: Up to 9 months per grant, renewable once

sources.title: A new short-stay visa for teleworkers

routes.tax_note: Foreign-source income is not taxable in Panama (per Mondaq).

open_questions: Qualified Investor: sources conflict on the legal instrument and date of the rise to USD 500,000 (Decree 17 of 8 September 2026, effective 16 September, vs 15 October 2026); check the Gaceta Oficial and the Servicio Nacional de Migracion.
Friendly Nations: the list of eligible countries (which EU states are included) and the 2026 changes were not read in an official source.
Government fees for all routes were not sourced from an official page; left null.
Pensionado and short-stay remote worker figures come from secondary sources.
Panama has no ordinary work-permit entry: not researched.
Naturalisation: the 5-year rule and the dual-citizenship position are from law-firm pages; the Constitution and Electoral Tribunal were not read.
